title: Every car in my game is timed to just miss you if you stay on the line. 37 attempts vs. the perfect run. Does that come across in the video?
author: CRHLR
selftext:
Last week a couple of people said my game looked like random cars, so I tried showing it differently.

The idea: every car is choreographed. If you stay on the line and keep in time, they all just barely miss you. Drift off it or get ahead or behind and something hits you. The overhead part is all 37 of my attempts at one level played back together, then the perfect run over the same stretch.

I built it with Claude Code, mostly in Unity. It’s free and plays in the browser, on keyboard or phone: [https://rom838.itch.io/ictus](https://rom838.itch.io/ictus)

Mostly I’d like to know: does the idea come across from the video, or does it still look random? And if you play it, where did you die and did it feel fair?

Part of me wants it that obvious so dying always feels like your fault but I get that it might make it doesn't fit the scene as well. Thanks for the mock-up! comments.author: SooooooMeta
comments.body:
I liked the overhead view because the premise is interesting.

As soon as it switched to first person my brain was unwilling to accept dozens of random cars driving onto the road from cornfields at random angles.

replies.author: CRHLR
replies.body: That's really helpful, thanks! I think you're right. Cars coming out of the fields is something I need to fix. I used to have every car on a road but then the roads were all over the place and looked crazy. I'll have to think more about this. Thanks again!

comments.author: RickRelentless
comments.body: Why do the other cars just come out of the middle of the desert? I get it on a gameplay level, but it makes zero sense from visual / ‘immersion’ point of view. I’d adjust your setting/theming so it fits your mechanic better and you get the ‘more than the sum of its parts’ effect.

replies.author: CRHLR
replies.body: Thanks for that feedback! You’re not the only one to mention it so you're definitely on to something. I'll have to think more about what would work best in the wordl. Appreciate you putting it that way. It’s a helpful way to think about it.

comments.author: Icaruslewis
comments.body: What's the point though? The player is just expected to "execute perfectly" to get a pre determined outcome, so theyre not even solving the problem themselves. Wouldn't it be better to remove the line but show previous attempts so the player can iteratively work out a route through? Kind of like Tom Cruise in Edge of Tomorrow.

replies.author: CRHLR
replies.body: That's a good question. It really is closer to a rhythm game than a puzzle/figuring things out game. More like Guitar Hero where the game tells you every note and the challenge is hitting them all. In this game the line tells you where to be, and the hard part is staying on it and on time while cars are flying at you and almost missing. But that said, the Edge of Tomorrow idea is *really* interesting. The game already records every attempt the player makes (that’s where the overhead footage came from) so a mode with no line where you learn from your old runs might actually be doable. I'm definitely gonna look into it. Thanks for this!

comments.author: DM_me_goth_tiddies
comments.body:
I think the area of the line just ahead of the car should be colour coded for speed. It’s not if you stick the line, it’s if you get the line at the right time. 

I would replace the line with chevrons and I would colour code the next chevron if you need to speed up or slow down.

replies.author: CRHLR
replies.body: Oh wow that's a really interesting idea! I think that could actually work well. So you're thinking if you get behind in time, the chevron would be colored to indicate that you should speed up? That's a cool idea. Right now the line is colored when the track requires you to speed up or slow down to stay in time, regardless of where you actually are in time. But a more variable line color is a good idea

comments.author: CRHLR
comments.body: Oh okay that's good to know. Yeah I had the other cars more transparent in an earlier version. But maybe I'll bring it back. Thank you for the feedback!

comments.author: CRHLR
comments.body: This is good feedback! Did it feel tough to control on the keyboard? Was there a specific part that didn't feel good? I actually do 90% of my play testing on the keyboard but I agree that it is much nicer with a controller. It is kinda like trying to play mario kart with a keyboard lol. I really appreciate you sharing your thoughts!
